definition: Fraught means filled or loaded with something difficult, tense, or dangerous — almost always in the pattern 'fraught with ___'
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word fraught. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know fraught should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Fraught means filled or loaded with something difficult, tense, or dangerous — it almost always appears in the pattern 'fraught with.' The peace negotiations were fraught with mistrust, and both delegations nearly walked out twice.
A tricky situation has a few snags to work around; a fraught one is loaded with tension at every turn.
A fraught crossing is loaded with risk; a perilous one puts lives in immediate danger.

Laden means weighed down with a heavy load, and the load can be anything — a ship laden with cargo, a table laden with food, a voice laden with meaning. Fraught takes only one kind of cargo: trouble. A fraught situation is loaded with tension, risk, or danger, never with anything welcome.

Charged describes an atmosphere crackling with suppressed emotion, like static before a storm — a charged silence, a charged glance. Fraught is broader about the trouble it carries: a situation can be fraught with risk, delays, or danger with no emotion in the room at all. Charged means feeling; fraught means trouble of any kind.

Riddled means shot through with flaws that are already there — a report riddled with errors, a wall riddled with holes. Fraught looks forward as much as inward: a fraught crossing is loaded with what could go wrong. Riddled counts the defects present; fraught measures the trouble hanging over the whole undertaking.

The freight cars were loaded with grain — freight and fraught both grew from the same old word for a ship's cargo.
Fraught means filled or loaded with something difficult, tense, or dangerous — almost always in the pattern 'fraught with ___'
The family reunion was fraught with old grudges, and every toast seemed one wrong word away from an argument.
Fraught with tells you the gathering was loaded with tension — the old grudges filled the event the way cargo fills a ship, and the word warns you the load is a troublesome one.
Fraught nearly always travels with 'with' — fraught with danger, fraught with tension, fraught with risk.
Modern English also allows a bare use ('a fraught relationship'), where it simply means tense.
Either way, the load is always trouble: fraught never describes happy abundance.

For the engineers in mission control, landing night was the moment every choice of the last nine years came due.

The descent would be fraught with dangers nobody could fix from Earth: a parachute that had to open within six seconds, a heat shield already scarred by the long journey, dust storms circling the landing site.
A radio signal took fourteen minutes to arrive, so by the time the room heard anything at all, the rover would already be safe — or already lost.
The chief engineer kept a card above her console listing forty-one separate things that had to go right.
When the tone finally came through, steady and clear, she crossed out the last line on the card and let herself breathe.
